harbor_p14_001.speaker: narrator
harbor_p14_001.text: In the sixteenth week, watermarks became the harbor's new measure of height. Children held their hands against them and argued over which street had been deepest. Shopkeepers scraped salt from shelves. A carpenter carried a repaired door uphill with the solemnity of a funeral until its owner asked why he had hung the latch upside down. Yue heard the laughter from the contact room. The storm had stopped, but stopping was only the first part of an aftermath. Every object needed drying, every lost hour needed a source, and every frightened person seemed to want a different yesterday.

harbor_p14_002.speaker: narrator
harbor_p14_002.text: Ke Chun visited the work board with her bruised shoulder supported as the attendant instructed. Her abandoned tool bag had washed out of the skiff and had not been recovered. She owned the tools; the yard owned the skiff and its repair question. The distinction seemed clear to the clerk and unbearable to Ke, whose next job depended on a needle she could not buy this morning. Han explained the available ordinary work inquiry and the separate incident claim route. Ke said she was tired of routes. Then she copied both locations onto one paper and kept it dry.

harbor_p14_003.speaker: narrator
harbor_p14_003.text: The younger rescued worker, Tong, had stayed with his sister after the shelter closed its overnight receiving. He came to the same board and pretended not to see Ke. She called him over. They argued about who first suggested returning to the skiff. Tong said the tool bag was hers. Ke said he wanted his own jacket too. Neither detail excused the return, and neither deserved to disappear from the account. Yue sat at the intake table while the independent clerk took their statements separately. The storm had made them companions. Shame was making them strangers again.

harbor_p14_004.speaker: harbor_han_pei
harbor_p14_004.text: You do not have to agree about your memory before you speak to the reviewer. I will not write a shared story just because the two of you arrived together. Ke, your account can name the bag and Tong's jacket. Tong can explain what he heard and chose. The supervisor's clearance sheet is another source. We have a place for the difference. I know it would feel simpler if one person could take all the blame and the other could go home. It would be simpler for the page, perhaps, and worse for the answer.

harbor_p14_005.speaker: narrator
harbor_p14_005.text: Tong looked at the floor and asked whether the reviewer would send the account to every hiring yard. Han gave the actual privacy and notice terms, including what might be shared for the review and what would not be posted publicly. She promised no universal protection against gossip. Ke placed her paper on the table and asked for the next appointment date. Tong did the same after a long pause. Their accounts entered the proper custody with names. Outside, Ke told him she still wanted the jacket mentioned because the bag had become too convenient an explanation.

harbor_p14_006.speaker: narrator
harbor_p14_006.text: Yan encountered both workers beside the cleared lane. He asked about their care restrictions, not the content of their statements. Ke could do light dry stitching when the attendant approved it; Tong's bruising needed another review before lifting. A shop had posted an ordinary short task sorting canvas scraps at a table. Ke went to inquire about its actual terms. Tong wanted Yan to tell the shop he had been brave. The foreman said he could confirm the rescue happened and Tong was ashore. He would not turn a frightened transfer into a recommendation unrelated to the job.

harbor_p14_007.speaker: narrator
harbor_p14_007.text: Bo heard that answer and disliked it. Later he told Yan the young man needed somebody on his side. Yan asked which side meant helping him obtain work he could do and which meant inventing a story that would follow him. Bo kicked a pebble through the drying mud and said older people made generosity sound like a court summons. The foreman laughed despite himself. He offered to go with Tong to the care review if Tong wanted company. Bo considered this insufficiently grand, then carried the offer himself. Friendship could start with accompaniment before it acquired a speech.

harbor_p14_008.speaker: narrator
harbor_p14_008.text: At the packing room, the partners laid their soaked paper in a ruined pile and examined the damp cord separately. An Shou knew a maker who could assess the cord without pretending drying restored its original strength. They paid for that private assessment from the next contract's actual receipts, after agreeing the amount among themselves. He Ming wanted to spend all morning counting the damage. Zhou said they also needed to deliver the dry parcels. The merchant's receiver arrived under the contract inspection and accepted the protected batch. Money finally came in while the ruined paper remained plainly ruined.

harbor_p14_009.speaker: narrator
harbor_p14_009.text: The second contract paid thirty copper altogether. Its ordinary material purchases had been eight and its rented work space four. The remaining eighteen paid the same three partners six each. Two copper from those private wages, contributed by their agreement, bought the cord assessment and a small replacement wrapping bundle. No public reserve paid this business loss. After agreed one-copper contributions, He Ming and Zhou each kept five; An retained six. Zhou disliked paying again and liked knowing her choice had not become He Ming's generosity on her behalf.

harbor_p14_010.speaker: harbor_he_ming
harbor_p14_010.text: We can put the loss on a page and still be angry about it. I do not want the next batch priced as if our time were free because this one survived. If we take work tomorrow, it pays its own wrapping and the hours we actually give. We can use the sound cord only after the maker tells us what it can do. We should also decide who speaks to the room owner about the drain. I will come. I would like Zhou beside me, because she will remember the part I am tempted to soften.

harbor_p14_011.speaker: narrator
harbor_p14_011.text: The maker found the damp cord suitable for ordinary parcel tying after drying, but not for the heavier purpose the partners had originally intended. An Shou kept that limit with the stock. The room owner showed the drain cleaning entry from before the storm and the inspector's account of the exceptional backflow from the lane. He also admitted one outlet cover had been stuck longer than the written schedule suggested. The partners did not have to decide everything at his doorway. They described their loss, took the records he agreed to provide and sought the ordinary tenancy advice appointment.

harbor_p14_012.speaker: narrator
harbor_p14_012.text: Wu came by after her inland chimney cap had been repaired by the landlord's contracted mason. The family had returned to their own lease, with the neighbor helping carry the duck basket. He now claimed the duck was less troublesome than the loose chimney had been. Wu said the bird would hear this and raise its rent. She brought lunch for He Ming from the canteen at the ordinary customer price and paid for her own bowl. A future packing task might still suit her hours, but she had not quit the canteen to make the possibility feel real.

harbor_p14_013.speaker: narrator
harbor_p14_013.text: Fen's binder reopened fully after drying the lower shelves. Some paper had been spoiled, including three copied pages from a private customer whose originals remained elsewhere. The binder requested permission to make replacements from those originals and paid the actual copying work under the customer agreement. Fen received a new assignment instead of being asked to redo damaged work for nothing. She was proud enough to tell Aning. Then she caught herself explaining the entire contract before saying the simpler thing: she had done a useful job, and someone thought her hand worth paying for again.

harbor_p14_014.speaker: narrator
harbor_p14_014.text: Aning's aunt invited Fen to examine a vacant copying stool at the account shop. The opportunity was an ordinary paid trial, not an adoption or a promise of lifelong security. It required steady attendance and some arithmetic Fen had only begun to learn. Fen asked for a week to consider and took the written terms home. Luo Jian read them slowly over supper. He wanted his daughter close because they had only recently found one another. He wanted her to take the chance because his injured hands could not be her whole future. Both wishes made him quiet.

harbor_p14_015.speaker: narrator
harbor_p14_015.text: Yue met Luo the next morning buying a cheap pencil. He said the binder's sorting was manageable and the closed storm day had been paid according to the shop's existing temporary closure term. He had nearly asked Fen to decline the trial, then heard his own father's voice inside that wish. Yue asked what his father would have said. Luo answered that the world was dangerous and a daughter belonged beside people who knew her. He looked at the pencil. Those words could describe love or a locked door. He had not yet found better ones to say.

harbor_p14_016.speaker: harbor_he_ming
harbor_p14_016.text: My mother used to say the safest road was the one already under her feet. Then she traveled here with my brother and scolded me for treating every unfamiliar lane as a threat. Parents change their advice according to who is leaving. That does not make the love false. It makes the advice something we should examine. If Fen takes the trial, you can ask how she gets home and whether the hours fit. You can also tell her you will miss the old supper time. The second truth does not have to become the first rule.

harbor_p14_017.speaker: narrator
harbor_p14_017.text: Luo laughed and asked whether He Ming's mother had given her permission to become so wise. She said her mother had given her permission to stop writing letters full of instructions. The joke made him breathe more easily. He bought the pencil and went to the binder, where paper waited for hands that could sort without gripping heavily. He Ming walked toward the partnership room with a letter from He Jun in her pocket. She had not opened it yet. Advising somebody else about family had been easier than reading what her own brother actually wanted.

harbor_p14_018.speaker: narrator
harbor_p14_018.text: He Jun's letter said their mother was well at Willow Reach and had decided not to visit again before the cold. Her own neighbors and familiar garden mattered more than He Ming's new harbor room. Jun had accepted another inland repair job with wages and a bounded term. He wanted to send their mother a share himself. He Ming had planned to send more from her partnership earnings, enough to prove the venture could carry her family. Now the letter asked for a conversation about actual needs rather than another parcel. She folded it badly and resented its sensible tone.

harbor_p14_019.speaker: narrator
harbor_p14_019.text: At the shelter room, the keeper returned the benches to their ordinary use after the last checked overnight group departed. One woman lingered because she preferred company to her own empty room. The keeper could offer the existing daytime gathering hour and the usual community meal location, not an indefinite emergency bed. Yue helped her understand the ordinary route during a scheduled half-day. The woman agreed to go home and asked Yue to walk as far as the corner after work. Yue did. Their conversation concerned a cat missing since the rain, a worry no public allocation could neatly conclude.

harbor_p14_020.speaker: narrator
harbor_p14_020.text: The cat appeared on the woman's doorstep before they did, wet and furious. She called it a traitor for frightening her and then carried it inside against its objections. Yue waited while she found a towel. On the wall hung a portrait of a husband who had died long before this storm. The woman said she knew what genuine loss looked like and still cried over the cat. Yue answered that knowing did not make the animal unimportant. The woman poured tea from an ordinary pot and did not ask the visitor to explain cultivation or the harbor's future.

harbor_p14_021.speaker: narrator
harbor_p14_021.text: Across the quay, Wen Zhi found water beneath two stacked tubs and a crack in the workshop door frame. The containers themselves were sound. Her late brother's maker marks looked darker when wet, as if somebody had recently cut them. She cleaned them with the cloth he once used and disliked the sudden memory. Peng Li had a paid repair slot available after his current job. Wen accepted the quote, then asked him to leave the old hinge if it still worked. He examined it and said it did. An original thing could remain without pretending damage had never happened.

harbor_p14_022.speaker: narrator
harbor_p14_022.text: Peng's plane came from the same lender who had approved its earlier use, under a renewed ordinary loan with a return day. Yue saw him carrying it wrapped against the remaining rain. He complained that the harbor was now full of doors wanting attention at the same time. She asked which door was least patient. He said every owner believed it was theirs. Wen overheard and said hers had been waiting decades for a carpenter with manners. The three of them laughed. Nobody needed the joke to settle the price or transfer a borrowed tool into anyone's permanent pack.

harbor_p14_023.speaker: narrator
harbor_p14_023.text: Deren's independent clerk brought him the next accident-review notice. The technical comparison had progressed, and the reviewer wanted his account of the last ordinary inspection he had witnessed before the platform failed. Deren remembered the patch being painted over, but he could not identify who authorized it. He said so. Yan's responsibility would be examined through his own role and the maintenance records, not filled out by a friend's suspicion. Deren found this difficult because he wanted his lost work resolved and wanted the foreman not to be hurt. He took both feelings to the appointment.

harbor_p14_024.speaker: narrator
harbor_p14_024.text: The clerk asked about Deren's immediate support separately from the later wage claim. Prescribed care had continued under the proper port injury process; he was not being asked to choose between speaking and receiving treatment. His compatible stock work paid its agreed hours. The disputed lost-work period still needed a result. Deren asked whether the review date would slip again because of storm duties. The office gave the current date and the person responsible for any change notice. It was an answer he could use. He wished it were the payment, then stopped himself apologizing for wanting money.

harbor_p14_025.speaker: harbor_yan_su
harbor_p14_025.text: He should want the money he actually lost. I do not like hearing that my check might be part of why he lost it, but those feelings cannot become his delay. I gave my account and the inspection sources. The reviewer will ask what follows from them. If I have to change my work or answer for a missed duty, I will. I am also allowed to hate waiting for the decision. Bo keeps telling me this in language too cheerful for my age. I asked him to stop, and he asked whether that was a safety instruction.

harbor_p14_026.speaker: narrator
harbor_p14_026.text: Bo's joke reached Deren, who sent back a message saying cheerful language was an occupational hazard Yan had chosen by hiring young people. The foreman smiled when he read it. Their friendship had not become evidence that the accident was forgiven. They could speak about soup and a foolish apprentice while a formal finding remained pending. Yue watched the note pass through the ordinary receiving room and thought how easily stories demanded one emotion at a time. Here affection and a claim for payment sat on the same bench, each taking room without making the other disappear.

harbor_p14_027.speaker: narrator
harbor_p14_027.text: The harbor master arranged the message trip only after pilots cleared the inner route. Six copper from the reserve's boat category carried closure updates and permitted family replies to the far collection point, returning the same afternoon. Yue's appointment ferry line paid none of this official warning work. A woman there learned that her hearing appointment would move to the inland room, with a named reader for the agreed hour. Her reply came back on the authorized circuit. Han received it as a request with a next step, not as proof that the far bank was now fully served.

harbor_p14_028.speaker: narrator
harbor_p14_028.text: The field route still had the reading gap discovered before the storm. Han used an approved portion of her office's ordinary staffing to arrange one bounded appointment for the woman who wanted help with a long letter. The appointment did not create a permanent keeper across the water. Yue read the returned source during her own scheduled work and saw the distinction matter: the letter described a household trying to separate peacefully, whose members did not want their addresses displayed. A public posting would have been easier and wrong. The permitted explanation took time, and somebody's actual duty covered it.

harbor_p14_029.speaker: narrator
harbor_p14_029.text: Rao Tong, the porter who had reported a split strap, received notice that his employment complaint had entered the competent review. His employer disputed the alleged threat to stop his pay. The review asked for the shift record and the person who heard the words. Yue had only seen the intake, and her statement said that. She could not become a witness to a conversation merely because she believed Rao was frightened. He told her he wanted belief and evidence together. She said she could offer the first personally and preserve the sources needed for the second. He accepted, unhappily.

harbor_p14_030.speaker: narrator
harbor_p14_030.text: Later Rao brought the name of a worker who had heard part of the exchange and agreed to speak under the stated process. He worried that the worker would lose the next shift. Han explained the review's actual protection and reporting route without promising every employer would behave well. The witness chose to proceed after hearing the terms. Rao sat on the back step afterward with a bowl he had bought and said the whole thing made him feel childish. Yue asked whether somebody threatening wages seemed childish to him. He said no. The answer let him finish eating.

harbor_p14_031.speaker: narrator
harbor_p14_031.text: The storm receiving desk closed after its last scheduled update and returned to the ordinary contact arrangement. Han removed the large temporary heading while leaving the referral dates visible. Her hand hesitated over the word located. It had stood above Niu's corrected address and had become, in rumor, a claim that the desk could find anyone. She changed the public explanation to identify what the desk actually received and confirmed. A fish seller passing outside said the smaller wording sounded less heroic. Han answered that Niu had spent the storm in a baker's room, which was heroic enough for him.

harbor_p14_032.speaker: narrator
harbor_p14_032.text: Sui attended the independent storm debrief with the harbor master, receiving keeper and crew representatives. Yue joined only for the part covering the contact work she had done. The master asked how two yard workers had returned after the clearance count. The supervisor described the first count, the missing exit confirmation and his assumption that the tool bag stayed aboard. Ke and Tong's separate statements supplied other choices. The debrief recorded a gap in the return barrier and notice routine. It did not declare that the rescued pair caused every loss in the yard because their return was vivid.

harbor_p14_033.speaker: narrator
harbor_p14_033.text: Yan admitted the protected bank kit had taken longer to reach the skiff than the rehearsal time suggested. A cart was parked across part of the approach, where its owner believed it had been cleared to wait. The parking instruction needed its source compared with the lane plan. Bo wanted the owner blamed immediately. The master asked who gave the instruction. A loader came forward with the old mark on his copy. The owner had followed it. The new clearance team had missed the conflicting page. An embarrassing administrative omission had become a physical obstruction before anybody noticed.

harbor_p14_034.speaker: harbor_sui_yan
harbor_p14_034.text: Put both copies beside the lane plan, and put the time they were issued beside them. We need the sequence before changing the routine. The owner moved the cart when directed; he did not choose to block a rescue. We also cannot call the delay harmless because both workers came ashore. The pilot's account says the second transfer narrowed the available margin. We will ask how the obsolete waiting mark survived the closure notice. I signed one of those notices. My signature belongs in this comparison with everybody else's, where somebody independent can read it.

harbor_p14_035.speaker: narrator
harbor_p14_035.text: The independent reviewer accepted the notice sources for the later port accountability file. Immediate repairs still needed doing. A hired pump cleared the last trapped water behind the shelter's approach, at six copper from the equipment category. Four authorized extra half-shifts at two copper cost eight for the final receiving and safe clearance work. The shelter's last checkable charges totaled twelve: six for overflow beds, four for meals and two for prescribed care supplies. With the six-copper message trip, the new reserve spending was thirty-two. Nothing in the debrief turned those receipts into a finding about who ultimately owed damages.

harbor_p14_036.speaker: narrator
harbor_p14_036.text: The safety reserve now had spent one hundred thirty and retained one hundred ten. Category balances were forty-four for shelter and care, twenty-six for equipment, twenty-two for extra shifts and eighteen for boats. Four unused stones remained secured; all four exhausted stones were logged separately from cash. The master released no stone purchase merely to restore a comforting round number. He requested a later readiness assessment under the proper procurement route. For the current quieter weather, ordinary clear lanes and staffed checks carried the work. Yue read the public status and then returned to the people waiting at her table.

harbor_p14_037.speaker: narrator
harbor_p14_037.text: One of those people was a messenger whose satchel had fallen into shallow water while he evacuated. He had retrieved it from a safe dry edge after the lane reopened, but three private letters were unreadable. The office could confirm the damage and contact their senders through the permitted route; it could not invent the words. One sender was dead, the recipient said. The letter had been old and carried between relatives rather than sent for the first time. Yue watched the man hold its blurred page. A fact could be recorded accurately and still leave something irreplaceable absent.

harbor_p14_038.speaker: narrator
harbor_p14_038.text: The recipient asked whether qi could bring the ink back. Yue explained the limits of her actual training and declined to test a wet private page with an unproven method. He looked disappointed, which she found harder than an accusation. Han offered the ordinary paper conservator's contact, with no guarantee of recovery and its actual fee terms. The man took it. After he left, Yue wanted to defend herself to the empty chair. Instead she opened the next request and discovered her hands were unsteady. She paused until the kettle's ordinary heat reached her fingers.

harbor_p14_039.speaker: harbor_han_pei
harbor_p14_039.text: You are allowed to dislike that answer. He is allowed to wish you had another one. We should not make either feeling into a story about what you owe. When I began this work, I thought a clerk's virtue was finding the sentence that made people leave satisfied. Some days the true sentence makes them leave grieving. I still want the other one. I do not think the wish will disappear with practice. The useful part is having somebody nearby who will stop us before we turn it into a promise.

harbor_p14_040.speaker: narrator
harbor_p14_040.text: Yue asked whether Han would stop her. The clerk said yes, provided Yue returned the favor when Han tried to describe a half-built contact route as finished. They shook hands over the kettle like merchants negotiating a ridiculous cargo. Then Han laughed at their solemn faces and fetched the bread she had bought privately. The loaf came from Sui's favorite baker, whose crust was crisp enough to make both of them complain. Their conversation wandered into the captain's failed baking. Neither woman sent that subject to a public board. Some truths belonged to the pleasure of knowing a friend.

harbor_p14_041.speaker: narrator
harbor_p14_041.text: That evening Sui attempted bread in her own room with her son's instructions. She had misread the resting interval before and was determined to obey it this time. Yue arrived by invitation just as the captain lifted the cover from dough that had risen beyond the bowl. Sui accused the bowl of lacking discipline. Her visiting neighbor said the dough had followed the instruction more faithfully than she had expected. They cleaned the ordinary spill together. The captain did not become charming because she could fail at bread. She was a tired woman making supper, and the failure was funny.

harbor_p14_042.speaker: narrator
harbor_p14_042.text: Sui's son had also asked whether she might visit his inland oven workshop before winter. She said the port calendar made it difficult. Yue asked what date he proposed. The captain read the letter again and realized he had offered three dates, not demanded the one she first rejected. She wrote a reply while the dough baked, giving one interval she could request through her roster. The visit still needed approval and travel money from her personal purse. Its possibility made her smile with embarrassment. She had been advising others about clear replies while sending her son vague refusals.

harbor_p14_043.speaker: narrator
harbor_p14_043.text: He Ming finally wrote back to He Jun about their mother. She asked the actual cost of the repair job's lodging and what their mother wanted for the cold months. She offered a bounded private contribution from her earned share, with no claim that it made her the family's decision keeper. The letter was less impressive than the parcel she had imagined sending. It also contained a page about the duck and Zhou's angry laughter, because her brother had asked what living at the harbor felt like. He had not asked for a statement of solvency.

harbor_p14_044.speaker: narrator
harbor_p14_044.text: Zhou found her sealing the letter and said she looked as if the paper had insulted her. He Ming admitted she had spent years accusing Jun of silence and now found his detailed wishes inconvenient. An Shou, sorting cord nearby, said the simplest solution was to have no relatives. Zhou asked whether he proposed to return his mother to the maker. They laughed, and An said his own mother would charge a handling fee. He Ming finished the letter. Humor did not resolve the family account. It gave her enough ease to send the question instead of another instruction.

harbor_p14_045.speaker: narrator
harbor_p14_045.text: Duan's painting yard reopened with one boat's fresh color streaked by rain that entered beneath a torn cover. The owner complained; the painter showed the contracted cover duty and her own preparation record, then agreed to compare the actual damage with him. Han came for her lesson and offered to help repaint for free. Duan refused to make goodwill part of a commercial repair dispute. They practiced on Han's own board instead. The clerk discovered she had wanted to be useful more than to paint. Duan told her usefulness was a poor substitute for learning where a line went.

harbor_p14_046.speaker: narrator
harbor_p14_046.text: Han tried the line again. It curved cleanly, then thickened where she pressed too hard. Duan made her keep that attempt rather than scrape it away. A board could show learning without becoming a public confession. Han carried it home under her coat and hung it beside the painted gull she already owned. Yue saw both when she came for tea. She liked the new curve more than the bird, which offended Han until Yue explained the line seemed made by somebody willing to continue. Han asked whether this compliment had a copying fee. They agreed on one more cup.

harbor_p14_047.speaker: narrator
harbor_p14_047.text: Fen visited Aning's shop after work to watch the trial stool in use. The current apprentice was leaving for a family business inland and described both the dull columns and the satisfaction of finding an error before a merchant did. Fen asked whether she would be scolded for slow arithmetic. The aunt said speed would develop; pretending to understand would be harder to repair. Fen took the example sheet home. Luo offered to practice sums with her and made the first mistake himself. They discovered they could laugh at a task without treating it as too small for courage.

harbor_p14_048.speaker: narrator
harbor_p14_048.text: The repair shed boy asked whether their fish kite should fly again now the sky had cleared. Fen said the paper needed a dry day and the tail had a torn tie. Aning fetched thread from her own scrap box, with permission from the aunt who owned the cloth remnants. The boy wanted all the names rewritten larger. Yue asked what had changed. He said he had worried nobody could see the passengers during the storm. Fen told him the names had stayed with the kite indoors. Some things survived without an audience, a thought he considered suspicious but useful.

harbor_p14_049.speaker: narrator
harbor_p14_049.text: At the far-bank reading appointment, the requested interpreter helped a woman explain the voluntary separation described in her long letter. Only the agreed receiving people learned the protected address. The household could ask about outstanding wages without being forced back into a shared home. Han received the bounded reply, and the ordinary office took the next payment-authority question. Yue saw how much of the work consisted of leaving an empty space where a story expected reunion. He Ming read the permitted status and said the woman sounded lonely. Han answered that loneliness was not permission to send somebody after her.

harbor_p14_050.speaker: narrator
harbor_p14_050.text: Shui Rong's contractor sent the written answer about the grounded barge's disputed interval. It offered payment for one part and denied another on the stated contract interpretation. The competent office arranged the comparison date; the crew could accept undisputed amounts without surrendering the remaining question under the documented terms. Shui asked for help reading the distinction. Han gave the ordinary referral, and He Ming accompanied her privately to the appointment. Their friendship did not transfer Shui's crew contract into the old wage guarantee. On the way home they bought roasted nuts and argued about which street smelled least of mud.

harbor_p14_051.speaker: narrator
harbor_p14_051.text: Luo Tai remained on the paid inventory task with the care and work limits already known to the contractor. His fear of losing later hiring had not vanished, but his wage arrived at its agreed date. He sent a remittance to his parents from his own earnings. Yue learned this when he asked whether the road posting was still open for replies. She gave the current location, not his family's address. He thanked her and said he might return to boat work after the next review. The sentence held a choice now, where the first one had held only fear.

harbor_p14_052.speaker: narrator
harbor_p14_052.text: The shore wall's damaged cap required a public maintenance crew with its own existing authorization. Yan supervised only the rigging task assigned within that job; the stonework belonged to the masons. Yue passed the site after her half-day and watched the workers argue cheerfully over a fitting block. Their tools came from the maintenance store, and the crew's water kettle sat well beyond the load boundary. One mason waved at her cup and said visitors should bring larger ones. She answered that he could charge rent for the water if he wanted. He laughed and filled it without a bargain.

harbor_p14_053.speaker: narrator
harbor_p14_053.text: Qin's beans survived unevenly. Two rows were gone, and a third looked unlikely to thank him for drainage. He replanted nothing immediately. Instead he sat in the garden with the replacement custodian, whom he had invited for tea rather than another lesson. They spoke about an old song both knew differently. When Yue brought a permitted office reply on her way past, the two men disputed the song's last line and asked her to judge. She had never heard it. Qin said this was a useful qualification for most judges. The custodian sang badly enough to end the argument.

harbor_p14_054.speaker: narrator
harbor_p14_054.text: The ordinary household desk received a new inquiry unrelated to the original thirteen references. Han opened it under its own source and time, without adding it retroactively to the completed voyage subtotal. Yue liked that the office could continue receiving people after one visitor's project closed. The new claimant was looking for an aunt who might simply have changed rooms. He had no wage question yet. The clerk gave the consent-aware contact route and asked what the aunt had last authorized him to know. The young man frowned, then admitted he had assumed a family relationship answered that by itself.

harbor_p14_055.speaker: narrator
harbor_p14_055.text: On her second scheduled half-day of the week, Yue compared referral dates with the actual receiving offices. One office had changed its room after storm damage. Its old sign still directed people down a wet stair. Han obtained the confirmed new location and had the public reference corrected during duty. A woman who had already walked to the wrong room called them careless. Han agreed the stale sign had cost her a journey and gave the appointment. The correction was useful; the woman's lost morning remained hers. Yue resisted explaining the storm as though it excused every later mistake.

harbor_p14_056.speaker: narrator
harbor_p14_056.text: Yue received four more copper for the week's two completed half-days. The six-copper bed and meal invoice brought the new term's spending to fifty-four, with one hundred forty-six remaining. Eight half-days had now been paid. No field fare or interpretation charge was added this week from her allocation; the independent appointments used their own offices' actual staffing. She copied only the totals needed for her personal account. The deeper change could not be totaled so neatly: she knew which friend's silence meant exhaustion, which joke hid worry, and where to sit without asking what the room was for.

harbor_p14_057.speaker: narrator
harbor_p14_057.text: At sunset Dai Min invited He Ming, Wu and Yue to see the repaired lamp shade she had made from an ordinary scrap frame. The lamp itself remained her privately purchased working tool. Wu's children came too and were told not to touch the hot glass. The younger one asked whether the light could keep the tide out. Dai said it could help a person see a knot, which was enough for this lamp. He Ming laughed at the answer, then looked around the room. Nobody there needed the light to become a miracle in order to enjoy it.

harbor_p14_058.speaker: narrator
harbor_p14_058.text: They ate a supper each household helped buy, with no public charge and no attempt to divide a spoonful into a moral account. Wu told the chimney story. Dai spoke of her husband without making the table stop eating. He Ming read one permitted sentence from Jun's letter and kept the rest private. Yue listened until the familiar cup was empty. The storm had altered their rooms and their expectations of one another. It had also left them an evening where the most urgent dispute concerned whether the buns were worth the baker's new price.

harbor_p14_059.speaker: narrator
harbor_p14_059.text: Yue ended the sixteenth week on the shore road, watching ordinary crews lift the last temporary barrier from a cleared section. The water had left a dark line on the wall above her shoulder. She touched nothing, only followed it with her eyes. Farther inland Han's room glowed behind a closed shutter, where the gull and the imperfect painted curve hung side by side. Yue turned toward her own lodging. Next week would bring trade again, and He Ming's partners had a proposal that sounded promising precisely because they already disagreed about it.
